section_summary: This section contains State Department records and FBI intelligence reports from March to September 1940 tracking Japanese attempts to purchase petroleum, iso-octane blending agents, and crude oil from American and British suppliers. Key investigations follow commercial negotiations involving Standard-Vacuum, Anglo-Iranian, Gulf Oil, and Japanese firms like Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha, alongside assessments of foreign agent registration and export controls. The section concludes with two background intelligence studies: a 1942 monograph detailing the social history and civil rights movements of Japan's outcast Eta (Burakumin) group, and a July 1940 psychoanalytic article by Kenji Otsuki analyzing perceived psychological shortcomings in the Japanese national character.

subfiles.about: Records a telephone inquiry from Standard-Vacuum regarding a quotation on iso-octane blending agent for the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: Green advised Kersey Coe that the State Department had no comment on the proposed 15,000-barrel blending agent quotation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Proposed Sale of Blending Agent to Japanese Navy

subfiles.about: Reports Standard-Vacuum's quotation through Mitsui & Company to supply hydropolymer blending agent to the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: Coe advised that Stanvac authorized its Yokohama office to quote on 15,000 barrels of hydropolymer subject to government protective clauses.
subfiles.title: Letter regarding Quotation on Blending Agent for the Japanese Navy

subfiles.about: Acknowledges blending agent negotiations and inquires into Standard-Vacuum's refining facilities in the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Green acknowledged the hydropolymer sale and requested data on petroleum and aviation gasoline refining facilities in Sumatra.
subfiles.title: Letter regarding Blending Agent Export and Inquiring into Netherlands East Indies Facilities

subfiles.about: Confirms acceptance of the hydropolymer tender and provides data on subsidiary refining capacity in Sumatra.
subfiles.summary: Coe reported the 15,000-barrel quotation was accepted and detailed NKPM Palembang refinery output and British Air Ministry contracts.
subfiles.title: Letter regarding Accepted Quotation and Netherlands East Indies Facilities

subfiles.about: Requests notification when hydropolymer shipments occur and acknowledges data regarding Netherlands East Indies refining facilities.
subfiles.summary: Green requested shipment dates for statistical records and appreciated information on refining capacity in the Dutch East Indies.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging Accepted Tender and Netherlands East Indies Information

subfiles.about: Explains the commercial background of Anglo-Iranian's sale of Iranian crude oil to Mitsubishi.
subfiles.summary: Jackson stated the 120,000-ton sale resulted from Iranian government revenue demands, refuting rumors of British-Japanese political rapprochement.
subfiles.title: Letter regarding Sale of Iranian Crude Oil to Mitsubishi

subfiles.about: Analyzes the diplomatic and commercial implications of the Anglo-Iranian crude oil contract with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Newspaper analysis examining whether the Iranian crude oil sale reflected Iranian revenue pressure or British-Japanese political rapprochement.
subfiles.title: Oil Deal by Tokyo and London Gets Tone on 1,000,000-Barrel Delivery From Iran

subfiles.about: Indexes statistical data concerning petroleum imports into Japan and Manchuria from 1937 through 1939.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet noting submitted figures on petroleum imports into Japan and Manchuria filed under 894.24/906.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Petroleum Imports into Japan and Manchuria

subfiles.about: Reports the contract volume increase and initial export of blending agent on a Japanese naval tanker.
subfiles.summary: Coe notified Green that 4,000 drums of blending agent were shipped from San Francisco on the Japanese tanker Kenyo.
subfiles.title: Letter Advising of Initial Shipment of Blending Agent to Japan

subfiles.about: Acknowledges notification of the initial shipment of hydropolymer blending agent aboard the Japanese tanker Kenyo.
subfiles.summary: Green acknowledged receipt of advice regarding the export of 4,000 drums of hydropolymer aboard the naval tanker Kenyo.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging Shipment of Blending Agent on Tanker Kenyo

subfiles.about: Transmits an FBI memorandum regarding negotiations by a Japanese corporation to purchase American aviation gasoline.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmitted a June 8 statement concerning aviation gasoline purchases by a Japanese company for the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.title: Cover Letter Transmitting Memorandum on Japanese Aviation Gasoline Purchase

subfiles.about: Details brokerage activities and meetings by Japanese representatives seeking aviation gasoline for naval use.
subfiles.summary: The FBI reported negotiations involving broker W. E. Logan, Hess Oil, and Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha representatives Matsuzaki and Schultz.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Japanese Negotiations for Aviation Gasoline

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the FBI's June 10 letter and memorandum regarding Japanese aviation gasoline purchases.
subfiles.summary: Berle thanked Hoover for transmitting the June 8 statement regarding aviation gasoline purchases for the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging FBI Statement on Japanese Aviation Gasoline Purchase

subfiles.about: Reports the departure of the Japanese tanker Toa Maru from Tuxpan carrying Mexican crude oil.
subfiles.summary: Consul Collins reported the tanker Toa Maru left Tuxpan for Shimotsu carrying 89,000 barrels of crude petroleum.
subfiles.title: Telegram regarding Japanese Tanker Toa Maru Crude Oil Shipment

subfiles.about: Transmits an FBI memorandum containing further details on Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha's gasoline negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmitted a June 15 memorandum containing comprehensive investigative data regarding Japanese aviation gasoline negotiations.
subfiles.title: Cover Letter Transmitting Follow-Up Memorandum on Japanese Gasoline Purchases

subfiles.about: Details investigation into brokers, banking transactions, and meetings between Japanese buyers and American oil executives.
subfiles.summary: The FBI investigated Logan, Milton Cohen, and Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha representatives. Gulf Oil confirmed meetings but denied entering into export contracts.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Investigation of Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha Gasoline Purchases

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the FBI's comprehensive memorandum of June 15 regarding Japanese fuel purchases.
subfiles.summary: Berle acknowledged Hoover's confidential letter and memorandum of June 15 concerning aviation gasoline purchases for the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging FBI Memorandum of June 15, 1940

subfiles.about: Transmits an investigative memorandum and inquires whether Japanese fuel buyers are registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act.
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwarded a memorandum and inquired whether Schultz, Matsuzaki, Yamaguchi, or Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha were registered foreign agents.
subfiles.title: Letter Inquiring regarding Foreign Agents Registration Status of Japanese Buyers

subfiles.about: Reports on alleged spot contracts, legal disputes, and overtures made to California refiners.
subfiles.summary: The FBI reported rumors of spot sales by Gulf Oil, Logan's planned litigation, and proposals to Wilshire Oil to construct a refinery.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Continuing Gasoline Purchase Negotiations by Schultz and Matsuzaki

subfiles.about: Advises the Department of Justice that the commercial activities of Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha representatives appear exempt from foreign agent registration.
subfiles.summary: The State Department informed the Attorney General that Schultz, Matsuzaki, and Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha fell within commercial exemptions of the 1938 Act.
subfiles.title: Note regarding Foreign Agents Registration Status of Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha Representatives

subfiles.about: Reports the transfer of Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha's letter of credit and an impending lawsuit by Logan.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reported a 500,000-dollar letter of credit was moved to Bank of America and Logan planned legal attachment for commissions.
subfiles.title: Letter regarding Transfer of Letter of Credit by Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Hoover's letter regarding the transfer of Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha's letter of credit.
subfiles.summary: Berle thanked Hoover for the confidential June 28 letter delivered by special messenger concerning aviation gasoline transactions.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging FBI Report on Letter of Credit Transfer

subfiles.about: Records the removal of a restricted document dated July 3, 1940 from the file.
subfiles.summary: GSA withdrawal notice for restricted document 894.3472/31 dated July 3, 1940, from Berle to Hoover.
subfiles.title: Withdrawal Notice for Item 894.3472/31

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese diplomatic conferences on iso-octane and Mitsubishi inquiries into California refinery capacities.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reported discussions with the Japanese Ambassador on iso-octane exports and Mitsubishi inquiries regarding California plant capacity.
subfiles.title: Letter regarding Japanese Ambassador Inquiries and Mitsubishi Iso-Octane Surveys

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Hoover's letter concerning Japanese aviation gasoline inquiries.
subfiles.summary: The State Department acknowledged receipt of the FBI's July 10 communication regarding Japanese aviation gasoline purchases.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging FBI Letter on Japanese Aviation Gasoline Purchases

subfiles.about: Transmits an investigative report from the FBI Pittsburgh Field Office regarding Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha and associates.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmitted Special Agent Hair's report concerning Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha, Perry Schultz, and Japanese representatives under the Neutrality Act.
subfiles.title: Cover Letter Transmitting FBI Report on Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha

subfiles.about: Summarizes interviews with Gulf Oil officials regarding renewed gasoline inquiries by Perry Schultz and Mitsubishi.
subfiles.summary: Agent Hair reported Gulf Oil declined to quote aviation gasoline to Perry Schultz because Mitsubishi had submitted a concurrent inquiry.
subfiles.title: Investigative Report on Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha, Perry P. Schultz, and Associates

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Special Agent Hair's investigative report on Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha and associates.
subfiles.summary: The State Department acknowledged Hoover's communication transmitting Agent Hair's report concerning Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha and Perry Schultz.
subfiles.title: Note Acknowledging FBI Report on Taiyo Sekiyu Kaisha

subfiles.about: Records the removal of a restricted document dated August 3, 1940 from the file.
subfiles.summary: GSA withdrawal notice for restricted document 894.3472/34 dated August 3, 1940.
subfiles.title: Withdrawal Notice for Item 894.3472/34

subfiles.about: Indexes correspondence and military opinions regarding aviation gasoline refining facilities in the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet noting Shell and Stanvac letters on Netherlands East Indies refining facilities, filed under 856d.6363/775.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Aviation Gasoline Facilities in the Netherlands East Indies

subfiles.about: Surveys the history, legal status, social discrimination, and civil rights movements of the outcast Eta community in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This monograph traces the origins of the Eta outcaste caste in ancient artisan slave classes and Shinto-Buddhist taboos against animal slaughter. It examines their legal emancipation in 1871, persistent social prejudices in employment and marriage, and the rise of the 1922 Suiheisha equalization movement under Umekichi Minami and Jiichiro Matsumoto. Finally, it analyzes living conditions in segregated settlements and modern group identity.
subfiles.title: A Short Account of the Eta: A Persecuted Group in Japan

subfiles.about: Presents a psychoanalytic critique of Japanese character traits, cultural symbols, and national behavioral patterns.
subfiles.summary: This translation of an article by psychoanalyst Kenji Otsuki analyzes Japanese national psychology through cultural objects such as the Rising Sun flag, kimono, and fundoshi. Otsuki outlines five principles governing Japanese behavior, asserting that the patriarchal family system produces child-like dependency, bureaucratic subservience, and an acute inferiority complex toward Western nations. He critiques militaristic glorification of death and uncritical imitation, arguing for genuine intellectual sublimation.
subfiles.title: Shortcomings in Japanese Character and Their Causes
